title: The whole people
hook: the Jewish people as one, beyond every movement

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: disagree with love. Hillel's students said the other side's view first. Did you try saying someone's view back to them? Today, the people the arguments happen inside. Day one thousand two hundred forty-five.

"And all the people answered together." That's the book of Exodus, at the foot of Mount Sinai. A crowd of former slaves, tired, unsure, some of them already complaining, and the text says they answered together. Not the elders for them. Not the best of them. All. Since this block began, we've counted streams: Orthodox and Haredi, Conservative and Reform, Reconstructionist, Renewal, Humanistic, secular, traditional, no label at all. Today steps back far enough to see them as one thing. There's a Hebrew phrase for that view from the mountain, and it's today's word.
screen: `ALL THE PEOPLE ANSWERED TOGETHER.` → `SO MANY STREAMS.` → `STEP BACK.`

segments.voice: Klal Yisrael. Klal means the whole, the general, everything together. Yisrael is Israel, the people. The whole people. Turn it four ways. First, the camp. Earlier in the same chapter, the text says, "there Israel camped before the mount." The medieval commentator Rashi noticed that in Hebrew the verb is singular: Israel camped, as one. He explained it: like one person, with one heart. On other days in the desert they quarreled. At Sinai they camped as one. Second, the answer itself: "All that the LORD hath spoken we will do." The covenant is made with a people, not a club of the most devoted. Third, what the phrase does today. When Jews use the phrase klal Yisrael, it points at something wider than any movement: the Jew in a black hat and the Jew who hasn't been to synagogue in years, the Jews of Morocco and of Ukraine, of Ethiopia and of Ohio. It is a way of saying that the arguments of this block happen inside a family, not between strangers. Fourth, the pull it creates. Some Jews feel klal Yisrael as a reason to keep a practice, so that Jews elsewhere can eat at their table or count them in their prayer. Others feel it as a reason to show up when Jews far away are in trouble. Different streams draw different lines on many questions. Klal Yisrael is the circle drawn around all of the lines.
screen: `KLAL: THE WHOLE.` · `ISRAEL CAMPED, AS ONE.` · `A COVENANT WITH A PEOPLE.` · `A CIRCLE AROUND THE LINES.` · then, large: `KLAL YISRAEL.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: think of Jews unlike you. Settle, and breathe. If you're Jewish, picture someone of your people who lives differently: another stream, another country, another language, another way of keeping Shabbat or not keeping it. Give them a face, a kitchen, a morning. If you're not Jewish, picture someone in your own community who prays, votes or lives very differently from you. Hold them in mind without arguing. Just let them be part of the whole. If you pray, you can include them in your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Klal Yisrael. The whole people of Israel, taken as one, wider than any movement, any country, any way of practicing. Today's word.
Your line: the whole people. Today, when you hear about someone very unlike you, notice the word us before the word them. Day one thousand two hundred forty-five.

howItsDone: Jews speak of klal Yisrael when they act for the Jewish people as a whole: supporting Jews in other countries, keeping practices that let others join them, and praying for Jews they will never meet.

notes: Rashi on Exodus 19:2 ('ke-ish echad be-lev echad') paraphrased; the singular verb (vayichan) claim comes from Rashi's comment. Confirm.
Klal = 'the whole, the general' is a translation, not an etymology; confirm pronunciation 'kih-LAHL' (often 'klahl').
Examples of Jewish communities (Morocco, Ukraine, Ethiopia, Ohio) are illustrative.
'Some Jews feel klal Yisrael as a reason to keep a practice' is a general description; confirm fair.
